Kit 6 di EVIL Scuola, secondaria di seco: EVIL for Schools kit 6, upper secondary: consent, image-based blackmail (sextortion), sharing of intimate photos and tools to get them taken down. A ready-made 50-minute lesson.
Nobody has the right to ask you for photos. You have the right to make them disappear.
Secondaria di secondo grado, classi 1ª–5: Upper secondary, ages 14–19 · 50 minutes · groups of 3–4
<strong>Da rivedere.</strong> Questo kit: Under review. This kit deals with a sensitive topic and is awaiting review by child safeguarding and helpline experts. Use it after talking to your school’s contact person.

Se qualcuno mi ricatta con una foto non: If someone blackmails me with a photo I don’t pay, I keep the evidence, I block and I ask for help: it isn’t my fault. If someone’s intimate photo reaches me, I don’t forward it. And there are tools to get it taken down.
Alla fine della lezione, gli studenti sa: By the end of the lesson, students can…
riconoscere pressione e ricatto: richies: recognise pressure and blackmail: insistent requests, threats, demands for money or more images;
conoscere le mosse da fare: non pagare,: know the moves: don’t pay, keep the evidence, block and report, talk to an adult or the police;
sapere che chi diffonde immagini intime: know that sharing intimate images without consent is a crime even if you only received them, and which tools help remove them.

Dai le regole: si parla di personaggi in: Set the rules: we talk about made-up characters, never real people or the school; nobody shares anything personal; anyone can pass. Write the sentence on the board and ask what it means.
<strong>Puoi dire:</strong> «“Nessuno ha: You can say: “‘Nobody has the right to ask you for photos. You have the right to make them disappear.’ Do you think it’s true? What does ‘right’ mean here?”
Leggi la storia: Sam, 16 anni, conosce o: Read the story: Sam, 16, meets a very friendly profile online. After a few days of compliments comes a request for a photo; then the threat: “Pay, or I send it to all your followers.” The class votes: pay so it ends; don’t pay, keep the evidence, block and ask for help; delete everything and tell nobody.
<strong>Puoi dire:</strong> «Pagare non: You can say: “Paying doesn’t end it: blackmailers who get money usually ask for more. Deleting everything loses the evidence and leaves you alone. The right move is the second, and the blame is always on the blackmailer, never on Sam.”
Gioco a gruppi: aiuta o fa danno?: Group game: does it help or harm?
Gruppi da 3–4: dividono le carte, che so: Groups of 3–4 sort the cards, which are actions, into the two columns. Then each group explains one card. Dwell on the actions of people who receive a photo: that’s where everyone can make a difference.
Proietta il livello «Per approfondire» d: Project the “Go deeper” level of stage 7 and present the tools: reporting to the Polizia Postale (the Italian police’s online crime unit), the preventive report to the Italian Data Protection Authority (on your own from 14) and Take It Down for images taken when under 18, which sends only a fingerprint of the file. Recall the law: sharing intimate images without consent is a crime even for those who only received them. And one firm rule: an intimate photo of a minor is never saved or forwarded, not even as evidence; save screenshots of the messages and threats, the profile name and the link. Hand out the anonymous tickets.
<strong>Puoi dire:</strong> «Il file res: You can say: “The file stays on your phone: Take It Down only receives a kind of fingerprint, which platforms use to recognise and remove the photo.”
Usa le domande qui sotto. Tieni il disco: Use the questions below. Keep the conversation on consent and on the responsibility of whoever shares, never on the choices of the person who sent a photo.
Ognuno completa il biglietto anonimo: un: Everyone writes on the anonymous ticket one thing they learned and, if they like, a question they didn’t ask in class; the tickets go in the box. Show the help numbers again.
<strong>Puoi dire:</strong> «Le quattro: You can say: “The four moves: don’t pay, keep the evidence, block and report, talk to someone. You’re never alone.”
<strong>Inoltrare a un amico la foto int: Forwarding a classmate’s intimate photo that arrived in the group to a friend Harms. Sharing it without consent is a crime even for those who only received it (Italian Criminal Code, art. 612-ter), and multiplies the harm.
<strong>Non inoltrarla, segnalarla alla: Not forwarding it, reporting it to the platform and telling an adult Helps. It stops the spread and brings in people who can get it removed.
<strong>Pagare chi ricatta perché smetta: Paying the blackmailer to make it stop Harms. It usually doesn’t stop: blackmailers who get money ask for more.
<strong>Salvare le prove (chat, profilo,: Saving the evidence (chat, profile, threats) before blocking Helps. The police (in Italy the Polizia Postale) need it, and it helps get content removed. Save messages, threats, profile and links: never an intimate photo of a minor, not even as evidence.
<strong>Cancellare tutto e non dirlo a n: Deleting everything and telling nobody Harms. The evidence is lost and you’re left alone with the problem.
<strong>Usare Take It Down per una foto: Using Take It Down for a photo taken when you were under 18 Helps. The file stays on your phone; participating platforms use the fingerprint to remove it.
<strong>Commentare «se l’è cercata»</str: Commenting “they asked for it” Harms. It shifts the blame onto the victim: the responsibility lies with whoever blackmails and whoever shares.
<strong>Scrivere alla persona: «Non è co: Writing to the person: “It’s not your fault. I’ll help you get help.” Helps. The person feels less alone and is more likely to talk to an adult.
Di chi è la colpa se una foto intima vie: Whose fault is it if an intimate photo gets shared?
<strong>Dove portare la classe:</strong>: Where to take the class: The fault lies with whoever shares it without consent, never with the person who took or sent it. Someone who received a photo in trust and forwards it commits a crime.
Perché chi ricatta chiede di non dirlo a: Why does a blackmailer ask you to tell no one?
<strong>Dove portare la classe:</strong>: Where to take the class: Because their power lies in shame and silence. As soon as you talk to an adult or the police, they lose their grip.
Cosa scriveresti a un amico a cui è succ: What would you write to a friend this happened to?
<strong>Dove portare la classe:</strong>: Where to take the class: Something like: “It’s not your fault. Don’t pay, keep the evidence, I’ll come with you to talk to someone.” And then you actually do it.
Se uno studente racconta qualcosa: If a student tells you something
Ascolta con calma e ringrazia per la fid: Listen calmly and thank them for trusting you. Don’t press with questions and don’t promise to keep it secret: explain that you’ll talk to someone who can help. Follow your school’s procedure and tell the bullying and cyberbullying contact person.
Nel biennio usa sei carte e lascia alla: With younger classes use six cards and keep the four moves and the help numbers on the board for the whole lesson.
Nel triennio leggete insieme l’art. 612-: With older classes read Article 612-ter of the Italian Criminal Code and the Data Protection Authority’s page on preventive reports together, and discuss consent in relationships.
Le carte si possono leggere in coppia; i: Cards can be read in pairs; the ticket can be completed with keywords. Nobody has to expose themselves in front of the class.
Proposta per casa, non obbligatoria: sal: Optional idea for home: save the local helpline numbers and the police reporting site in your contacts (in Italy 114, 1.96.96 and commissariatodips.it), and look at the Get help now page with an adult.
